                or path.stat().st_size != result["bytes"]
                or file_digest(path) != result["sha256"]):
            raise ValueError("The original comparison export changed before report capture")
        _bundle(path, selection)
        _copy_file(path, destination)
    context = verify(workspace, directory, selection)
    _bundle(destination, selection, target=directory / "native-comparison")
    if staging.exists():
        shutil.rmtree(staging)
    report("retain-budget-maps-and-scientific-context")
    maps = []
    for plan in context["plans"]:
        if plan["status"] in comparison.FEASIBLE:
            name = "maps/" + plan["id"] + ".svg"
            atomic_bytes(directory / name, _map_svg(context["network"], plan), immutable=True)
            maps.append(name)

"""Budget/coverage/strata/calendar-constrained monitoring network design.

MILP decisions select catchment search areas, not invented field coordinates.
Coverage is a disclosed planning objective, never a water-quality observation.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import math
import time
from typing import Any
import numpy as np
from scipy.optimize import Bounds, LinearConstraint, milp
from scipy.sparse import coo_matrix, vstack

from .monitoring_common import ContractError
from .monitoring_network import coverage_sets, existing_coverage, graph_distances, number
from .monitoring_campaign import (integer, money_cents, dollars, cost_table,
                                  calendar_site_capacity, build_calendar)


def ids(value: Any, name: str, universe: set[str]) -> set[str]:
    if not isinstance(value, list) or any(not isinstance(v, str) for v in value):
        raise ContractError(f"{name} must be an array of string IDs")
    result = set(value)
    if len(result) != len(value):
        raise ContractError(f"{name} contains duplicate IDs")
    unknown = result - universe
    if unknown:
        raise ContractError(f"{name} contains unknown IDs: {sorted(unknown)}")
    return result


def solve_design(network: dict, config: dict) -> dict:
    """Return a complete feasible design or an explicit infeasible/limited result.

    A successful incumbent is re-evaluated in integer cents and graph sets. It
    is never labelled optimal unless the solver closes the selected gap.
    """
    started = time.perf_counter()
    nodes = network["nodes"]
    keys = sorted(nodes)
    index = {key: i for i, key in enumerate(keys)}
    universe, n = set(keys), len(keys)
    mode = config.get("coverage_mode", "local")
    coverage = coverage_sets(network, mode)
    existing_ids = config.get("existing_station_ids", [])
    baseline = existing_coverage(network, mode, existing_ids)
    required = ids(config.get("required_ids", []), "required_ids", universe)
    excluded = ids(config.get("excluded_ids", []), "excluded_ids", universe)
    if required & excluded:
        raise ContractError(f"required and excluded overlap: {sorted(required & excluded)}")
    calendar_config = config.get("calendar")
    if not isinstance(calendar_config, dict):
        raise ContractError("a complete calendar configuration is required")
    calendar_capacity = calendar_site_capacity(calendar_config)
    costs, breakdown = cost_table(network, config, calendar_config)
    overhead = money_cents(config.get("program_overhead", "0.00"), "program_overhead")
    budget = money_cents(config.get("budget"), "budget")
    max_sites = integer(config.get("max_sites", n), "max_sites")
    min_sites = integer(config.get("min_sites", 0), "min_sites")
    max_sites = min(max_sites, n, calendar_capacity)
    separation = integer(config.get("minimum_network_separation", 0), "minimum_network_separation")
    separation_pairs = graph_distances(network, separation)
    explicit_pairs = config.get("incompatible_pairs", [])
    if not isinstance(explicit_pairs, list):
        raise ContractError("incompatible_pairs must be an array of ID pairs")
    for pair in explicit_pairs:
        if not isinstance(pair, list) or len(pair) != 2:
            raise ContractError("each incompatible pair must contain two distinct catchment IDs")
        checked = ids(pair, "incompatible pair", universe)
        if len(checked) != 2:
            raise ContractError("an incompatible pair must contain two distinct IDs")
        separation_pairs.add(tuple(sorted(checked)))
    strata = config.get("minimum_by_stratum", {})
    if not isinstance(strata, dict):
        raise ContractError("minimum_by_stratum must be an object")
    strata = {str(key): integer(value, f"minimum_by_stratum.{key}") for key, value in strata.items()}
    known_strata = {v["stratum"] for v in nodes.values()}
    if set(strata) - known_strata:
        raise ContractError(f"unknown strata: {sorted(set(strata) - known_strata)}")
    time_limit = number(config.get("time_limit_seconds", 120), "time_limit_seconds", minimum=0.01)
    gap = number(config.get("relative_gap", 0), "relative_gap")
    if gap > 1:
        raise ContractError("relative_gap must be between 0 and 1")
    warnings = []
    if network["station_assignment_issues"]:
        warnings.append("Source station assignment issues remain; only explicitly chosen assigned stations contribute to coverage.")
    preliminary = []
    if overhead > budget:
        preliminary.append("fixed program overhead exceeds total budget")
    if min_sites > max_sites or len(required) > max_sites:
        preliminary.append("minimum/required site count exceeds site or calendar capacity")
    if sum(costs[k] for k in required) + overhead > budget:
        preliminary.append("required sites and overhead exceed the campaign budget")
    if any(a in required and b in required for a, b in separation_pairs):
        preliminary.append("required sites violate a separation or incompatibility constraint")
    for stratum, minimum in strata.items():
        available = sum(k not in excluded and nodes[k]["stratum"] == stratum for k in keys)
        if minimum > available:
            preliminary.append(f"stratum {stratum!r} needs {minimum} sites but only {available} are eligible")
    base_result = {"schema": "eco.monitoring.design/1", "configuration": config,
                   "network_id": network.get("id"), "source_bindings": network["source_bindings"],
                   "coverage_mode": mode, "weight_basis": network["weight_basis"],
                   "coverage_meaning": ("catchment-level planning presence" if mode == "local" else
                       "potential upstream context at a proposed outlet; not guaranteed observation representativeness"),
                   "calendar_site_capacity": calendar_capacity,
                   "existing_station_ids": existing_ids, "baseline_covered_ids": sorted(baseline),
                   "warnings": warnings}
    if preliminary:
        return {**base_result, "status": "infeasible", "diagnostics": preliminary, "selected_ids": [],
                "elapsed_seconds": time.perf_counter() - started}

    # x_i: selected catchment. z_i: uncovered target newly represented.
    # Continuous z in [0,1] is sufficient with binary x and nonnegative weights.
    rows, columns, values, lower, upper = [], [], [], [], []
    def constraint(terms: dict[int, float], lo: float = -np.inf, hi: float = np.inf):
        r = len(lower)
        for col, value in terms.items():
            if value:
                rows.append(r); columns.append(col); values.append(value)
        lower.append(lo); upper.append(hi)
    constraint({index[k]: costs[k] for k in keys}, hi=budget - overhead)
    constraint({i: 1 for i in range(n)}, lo=min_sites, hi=max_sites)
    for stratum, minimum in strata.items():
        constraint({index[k]: 1 for k in keys if nodes[k]["stratum"] == stratum}, lo=minimum)
    for a, b in sorted(separation_pairs):
        constraint({index[a]: 1, index[b]: 1}, hi=1)
    target_sources = {key: [] for key in keys}
    for site, targets in coverage.items():
        for target in targets:
            target_sources[target].append(index[site])
    for key in keys:
        if key not in baseline:
            constraint({**{i: -1 for i in target_sources[key]}, n + index[key]: 1}, hi=0)
    lo = np.zeros(2 * n)
    hi = np.ones(2 * n)
    for key in required:
        lo[index[key]] = 1
    for key in excluded:
        hi[index[key]] = 0
    for key in baseline:
        hi[n + index[key]] = 0
    weights = np.array([number(nodes[k]["weight"], f"weight {k}") for k in keys])
    # Normalize only for numerics. Objective/report remain original source units.
    if not math.isfinite(float(weights.sum())):
        raise ContractError("combined priority weights exceed finite numeric range")
    scale = max(float(weights.sum()), 1.0)
    objective = np.concatenate((np.zeros(n), -weights / scale))
    matrix = coo_matrix((values, (rows, columns)), shape=(len(lower), n * 2)).tocsc()
    integrality = np.concatenate((np.ones(n, dtype=int), np.zeros(n, dtype=int)))
    options = {"time_limit": time_limit, "mip_rel_gap": gap, "presolve": True}
    constraints = LinearConstraint(matrix, np.array(lower), np.array(upper))
    answer = milp(objective, integrality=integrality, bounds=Bounds(lo, hi), constraints=constraints, options=options)
    if answer.x is None:
        return {**base_result, "status": "infeasible" if answer.status == 2 else "no_feasible_incumbent",
                "solver": {"status": int(answer.status), "message": str(answer.message)},
                "diagnostics": ["Joint constraints have no feasible design." if answer.status == 2 else str(answer.message)],
                "selected_ids": [], "elapsed_seconds": time.perf_counter() - started}
    first = answer
    tie_status = "not-run"
    # Secondary cost solve only after the primary closes its requested gap.
    # The original incumbent is retained if secondary optimization is interrupted.
    if answer.status == 0:
        remaining = time_limit - (time.perf_counter() - started)
        if remaining > 0.02:
            achieved = float(-answer.fun)
            bound_matrix = vstack((matrix, coo_matrix((-objective).reshape(1, -1))), format="csc")
            cost_scale = max(sum(costs.values()), 1)
            second_objective = np.concatenate((np.array([costs[k] / cost_scale for k in keys]), np.zeros(n)))
            second = milp(second_objective, integrality=integrality, bounds=Bounds(lo, hi),
                          constraints=LinearConstraint(bound_matrix, np.r_[lower, achieved - 1e-10], np.r_[upper, np.inf]),
                          options={"time_limit": remaining, "mip_rel_gap": 0.0, "presolve": True})
            tie_status = "optimal" if second.status == 0 else "incomplete"
            if second.x is not None:
                proposed = [keys[i] for i in range(n) if second.x[i] > 0.5]
                original = [keys[i] for i in range(n) if first.x[i] > 0.5]
                def coverage_weight(selected):
                    covered = set(baseline)
                    for key in selected: covered.update(coverage[key])
                    return sum(nodes[k]["weight"] for k in covered)
                # Check primary objective on discrete source sets, not solver z tolerances.
                if coverage_weight(proposed) >= coverage_weight(original) - 1e-9 and sum(costs[k] for k in proposed) <= sum(costs[k] for k in original):
                    answer = second
                else:
                    tie_status = "discarded-numerical-tolerance"
    selected = sorted(keys[i] for i in range(n) if answer.x[i] > 0.5)
    chosen = set(selected)
    # Exact postsolve checks: no floating point tolerance can spend extra cents.
    spent = sum(costs[k] for k in selected) + overhead
    violations = []
    if spent > budget: violations.append("budget")
    if not min_sites <= len(chosen) <= max_sites: violations.append("site count")
    if required - chosen or chosen & excluded: violations.append("required/excluded")
    if any(a in chosen and b in chosen for a, b in separation_pairs): violations.append("incompatibility")
    if any(sum(nodes[k]["stratum"] == s for k in chosen) < v for s, v in strata.items()): violations.append("stratum minimum")
    if violations:
        raise ContractError(f"solver incumbent failed exact validation: {', '.join(violations)}")
    total_coverage = set(baseline)
    contributions = []
    # Deterministic marginal accounting for display. MILP optimizes all sites jointly.
    for key in selected:
        marginal = coverage[key] - total_coverage
        contributions.append({"id": key, "stratum": nodes[key]["stratum"],
                              "coverage_ids": sorted(coverage[key]), "marginal_ids": sorted(marginal),
                              "marginal_weight": sum(nodes[k]["weight"] for k in marginal),
                              "cost": breakdown[key], "geometry_role": "source-catchment-search-area"})
        total_coverage.update(coverage[key])
    total_weight = sum(node["weight"] for node in nodes.values())
    covered_weight = sum(nodes[k]["weight"] for k in total_coverage)
    station_set = set(existing_ids)
    return {**base_result, "status": "optimal" if first.status == 0 and gap == 0 else "feasible",
            "solver": {"engine": "scipy.optimize.milp / HiGHS", "primary_status": int(first.status),
                       "message": str(first.message), "requested_relative_gap": gap,
                       "achieved_relative_gap": float(first.mip_gap) if getattr(first, "mip_gap", None) is not None else None,
                       "minimum_cost_tiebreak": tie_status,
                       "nodes": int(first.mip_node_count) if getattr(first, "mip_node_count", None) is not None else None},
            "selected_ids": selected, "selected": contributions,
            "covered_ids": sorted(total_coverage), "uncovered_ids": sorted(universe - total_coverage),
            "coverage": {"covered_weight": covered_weight, "total_weight": total_weight,

                         "baseline_weight": sum(nodes[k]["weight"] for k in baseline),
                         "covered_catchments": len(total_coverage), "total_catchments": n},
            "cost": {"currency": config.get("currency", "USD"), "budget_cents": budget,
                     "program_overhead_cents": overhead, "total_cents": spent, "remaining_cents": budget - spent,
                     "total_display": dollars(spent), "scope": "new-site setup and all scheduled visits plus stated program overhead",
                     "existing_station_costs": "external baseline costs are excluded; add them to program_overhead when program-funded"},
            "calendar": build_calendar(selected, calendar_config),
            "elapsed_seconds": time.perf_counter() - started}


def solve_frontier(network: dict, config: dict, budgets: list[str]) -> dict:
    if not isinstance(budgets, list) or not budgets:
        raise ContractError("frontier budgets must be a nonempty array")
    cents = [money_cents(value, "frontier budget") for value in budgets]
    if len(set(cents)) != len(cents):
        raise ContractError("frontier budgets must be distinct")
    # All requested budgets are executed, not sampled or silently truncated.
    designs = [solve_design(network, {**config, "budget": dollars(value)}) for value in sorted(cents)]

                      "total_cost": design.get("cost", {}).get("total_display"),
                      "selected_ids": design["selected_ids"]} for design in designs]}

# Carry a Monitoring campaign into fieldwork

Open **Monitoring design**, choose the saved campaign in **Campaign fieldwork**,
and select **Update fieldwork from this revision**. The existing native task queue
retains that exact campaign revision. When it completes, **Open saved fieldwork**
opens its saved Implementation revision. The original source package is available
from both the completed task and the plan's managed attachments.

The same campaign always selects the same Implementation plan. A later campaign
revision updates the generated fields that still match the previous source
edition. Local fieldwork edits are preserved and the saved result identifies each
incoming change that was kept for review. Every received campaign edition remains
a frozen source link, with its complete native source package.

## Original data carried through

- Each selected catchment remains a search area until the saved campaign binds an
  actual source station. Coordinates come from that station's original WGS84 point.
- Visits retain original dates, local start and finish times, rounds and crews.
  Local wall times stay local; the adapter does not assign a timezone.
- The associated task keeps its planned start date and original crew. Its duration
  is unset because the Monitoring calendar expresses visit minutes, while the
  Implementation task scheduler uses whole working days.
- A collected event supplies its original sample ID and actual timestamp. Sample
  activities retain the complete original values object and original event ID.
  Lab measurements use the existing Implementation lab import mapping.
- The original design's total USD cents become a planning budget line. Its
  breakdown and scope stay attached to that line.
- Source revisions, design, network, field history, original vector sources and
  their companions are retained in the managed monitoring field package.

Monitoring missed visits remain open fieldwork with the original missed status
and note. Cancelled visits retain cancellation; completed visits require the
original collected-event timestamp. An earlier sample at a different station
retains its own source-backed historical visit and coordinates.

## Receiving a revised campaign

The importer compares each generated field with its previously imported value.
An unchanged generated field follows the new source edition. A field edited in
Implementation remains as edited, and the incoming value appears in
`monitoring_origin.preserved_fieldwork_changes` alongside the new frozen source.

Unmodified, still-planned generated visits and tasks removed by a revised design
move into `monitoring_superseded_rows`. Actual samples, their referenced visits,
and edited work remain retained. Historical monitoring-plan memberships keep
their original site sets. The current design's budget replaces its prior
generated budget when that amount remains unedited.

An already received source revision reuses the saved plan and its attachment.
A historical campaign edition can be attached after a newer one without moving
the current generated fieldwork backwards. Replaying a task after an interrupted
attachment resumes from the saved source selection.

## Native integration

The registered queued action is `monitoring.campaign.fieldwork`, with the existing
workspace key and payload:

```json
{
  "campaign_id": "<original campaign ID>",
  "expected_revision_id": "<selected original revision ID>",
  "operation_id": "<retained client operation ID>"
}
```

The original Monitoring transport retains the operation ID across a lost reply.
The result identifies the saved Implementation plan/revision, current source
edition, counts, preserved edits and managed source attachment. The regular task
view links to `implementation_plans`; the registered desk uses
`openSavedPlan({workspace_key, plan_id, revision})`.

The complete native Implementation report and Project transfer workflows then
carry this same plan, revision history, attached sources and retained reports
through independent reopening. Existing Monitoring design, observed-context,
source-network and lab-import components continue through their original APIs.

Generated visit and task identities include their original design ID. A changed
design retains collected samples against their original calendar, while its new
planned work uses the new saved design. Site identities include the original
network edition, preserving historical station coordinates after a source change.

## Linked fieldwork edits

Campaign updates preserve deleted visits and sites together with their dependent incoming tasks and samples. Changes that cannot join the retained fieldwork graph are retained in `preserved_fieldwork_changes` and the attached source package. Existing sample sites protect their original visit, and monitoring-plan membership keeps local members while admitting all retained visit sites. The packet contains every original design, network and publisher source referenced by its selected campaign history.

"""Original native evidence beside explicit Sampling targets.

TokenJunkieLabs. Frozen scientific sources support analyst-authored sampling
questions. This adapter computes no model, information gain or target priority.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

from copy import deepcopy
from pathlib import PurePosixPath

from .common import digest, identifier, read_json, verify_file
from .monitoring_common import ContractError, canonical_bytes

SCHEMA = "upstate.monitoring-native-evidence/v1"
FAMILIES = {
    "multivariate_control_outcomes_id": ("control_outcomes", "urn:upstate:multivariate-control-outcomes:"),
    "terrain_conditioning_report_source_id": ("terrain_response", "urn:upstate:terrain-conditioning-report-source:"),
}
LIMITATIONS = [
    "This is retained native-model evidence supporting an analyst-authored sampling question; no information gain, target priority or statistical power is calculated.",
    "The source's modeled support is not established as this station's contributing catchment. Original station, network and catchment assignments are retained without inferring equivalence from names or identifiers.",
    "Annual modeled source-pixel exports to streams are not station concentrations or intake loads. No flow conversion, calibration or annual-to-seasonal allocation is performed.",
    "The exact observed characteristic, fraction, speciation, method and unit remain distinct. A modeled nitrogen, phosphorus or sediment quantity does not establish equivalence to nitrate, dissolved fractions, orthophosphate or suspended-solids measurements.",
    "Several deterministic control placements or terrain variants are sensitivity evidence, not independent observed replicates, probabilities or confidence intervals.",
]


def normalize(value):
    if not isinstance(value, dict) or set(value) != {
            "source_collection_id", "source_id", "pollutant", "applicability"}:
        raise ContractError("Choose one exact native report source, quantity and authored applicability")
    result = {"source_collection_id": identifier(value["source_collection_id"])}
    for key in ("source_id", "pollutant", "applicability"):
        text = value.get(key)
        if not isinstance(text, str) or not text.strip() or len(text) > (20000 if key == "applicability" else 300):
            raise ContractError("Retain the exact native evidence " + key)
        result[key] = text if key == "source_id" else text.strip()
    if _name(result["source_id"]) != result["source_id"] or "/" in result["source_id"]:
        raise ContractError("Retain a portable original source entry ID")
    return result


def _name(value):
    if not isinstance(value, str):
        raise ContractError("A native evidence member needs its original relative name")
    path = PurePosixPath(value)
    if (path.is_absolute() or not path.parts or str(path) != value
            or ".." in path.parts or "\\" in value or "\0" in value):
        raise ContractError("A native evidence source member is not portable")
    return value


def _document(workspace, collection_id, source_id):
    collection = workspace._get("sources", identifier(collection_id))
    entries = [e for e in collection["entries"] if e["id"] == source_id]
    if len(entries) != 1:
        raise ContractError("Choose an exact retained native evidence entry")
    entry = entries[0]
    if entry.get("kind") != "document" or entry.get("role") != "OBSERVED_CONTEXT":
        raise ContractError("Native evidence must be an original scientific report document")
    metadata = entry.get("metadata", {})
    if not isinstance(metadata, dict):
        raise ContractError("The selected native evidence needs original typed source metadata")
    families = [(key, spec) for key, spec in FAMILIES.items() if key in metadata]
    if len(families) != 1 or metadata.get("report_schema") != "upstate.observed-report/v1":
        raise ContractError("Choose a supported completed native outcome or terrain report")
    key, (family, prefix) = families[0]
    native_id = identifier(metadata[key])
    if entry.get("uri") != prefix + native_id:
        raise ContractError("The native report URI differs from its retained identity")
    bodies, paths = {}, {}
    companions = entry.get("companions", [])
    if not isinstance(entry.get("body"), dict) or not isinstance(companions, list) or any(not isinstance(v, dict) for v in companions):
        raise ContractError("The native evidence source needs complete body and companion descriptors")
    for body in [entry["body"], *companions]:
        name = _name(body.get("view_path", body["filename"]))
        if name in bodies:
            raise ContractError("The native scientific source repeats an original member")
        bodies[name] = deepcopy(body)
        paths[name] = verify_file(workspace.root, {**body, "path": body["object"]})
    recipe = read_json(paths[_name(entry["body"].get("view_path", entry["body"]["filename"]))])
    if recipe.get("schema") != "upstate.observed-report/v1":
        raise ContractError("The original report recipe has an unsupported schema")
    expected = {}
    for member in recipe.get("inputs", []):
        name = _name(member["path"])
        if name in expected:
            raise ContractError("The native recipe repeats an original companion")
        expected[name] = (member["bytes"], member["sha256"])
    actual = {_name(body.get("view_path", body["filename"])): (body["bytes"], body["sha256"])
              for body in entry.get("companions", [])}
    if expected != actual:
        raise ContractError("The complete native evidence companion inventory differs from its recipe")
    if recipe.get("project_id") != metadata.get("project_id"):
        raise ContractError("The native evidence project differs from its original source")
    source = {"collection_id": collection_id, "source_id": source_id,
              "collection_sha256": digest(collection), "entry_sha256": digest(entry),
              "body": deepcopy(entry["body"]), "members": deepcopy(entry.get("companions", [])),
              "title": entry.get("title", source_id), "uri": entry["uri"],
              "classification": deepcopy(metadata.get("classification"))}
    return collection, entry, paths, source, family, native_id, recipe


def _json(paths, name):
    if name not in paths:
        raise ContractError("Retain the native evidence companion " + name)
    return read_json(paths[name])


def _native(workspace, entry, paths, family, native_id, recipe):
    metadata = entry["metadata"]
    project_id = metadata["project_id"]
    local = project_id == workspace.project["id"]
    if family == "control_outcomes":
        value = _json(paths, "assessment.json")
        if (value.get("schema") != "upstate.multivariate-control-outcomes/v1"
                or value.get("id") != native_id or value.get("state") != "complete"
                or digest(value["identity"]) != native_id
                or value["identity"]["project_id"] != project_id
                or value["selection"] != value["identity"]["selection"]
                or value["binding"] != value["identity"]["binding"]
                or _json(paths, "selection.json") != value["selection"]
                or _json(paths, "input-binding.json") != value["binding"]):
            raise ContractError("The completed outcome evidence changed its original identity")
        if local:
            from . import multivariate_control_outcomes as original
            retained = original.inspect(workspace, native_id)
            if any(retained.get(k) != v for k, v in value.items()):
                raise ContractError("The selected report differs from its original native outcome")
        pollutants = value["selection"]["pollutants"]
        units = {}
        for region in value["regions"]:
            for pollutant, row in region["siting_contrasts"].items():
                if pollutant in units and units[pollutant] != row["units"]:
                    raise ContractError("One original native quantity has inconsistent annual units")
                units[pollutant] = row["units"]
        if set(units) != set(pollutants):
            raise ContractError("The native outcome evidence lost a selected quantity")
        classifications = []
        for member in value["binding"]["members"]:
            design = _json(paths, "originals/" + member["design_id"] + "/design.json")
            if (design.get("id") != member["design_id"]
                    or digest(design["identity"]) != member["design_id"]
                    or design["binding"] != design["identity"]["binding"]
                    or design["selection"] != member["selection"]):
                raise ContractError("The original design-source classification lost its retained identity")
            classifications.append({"design_id": member["design_id"],
                "selection": deepcopy(member["selection"]),
                "grid_sources": deepcopy(design["binding"]["grid_sources"]),
                "external_covariates": deepcopy(design["binding"]["external_covariates"]),
                "grid_inputs": deepcopy(design["binding"]["grid_inputs"]),
                "exclusion_source": deepcopy(design["binding"]["exclusion_source"])})
        result = {"family": family, "id": native_id, "project_id": project_id,
            "quantity_scope": value["selection"]["quantity_scope"],
            "quantities": [{"pollutant": p, "units": units[p]} for p in pollutants],
            "run_ids": list(value["binding"]["runs"]),
            "grid_id": value["binding"]["grid_id"], "profile_id": value["binding"]["profile_id"],
            "geometry": deepcopy(value["binding"]["grid_files"]),
            "rows": deepcopy(value["regions"]), "support": deepcopy(value["summary"]["group_common_support"]),
            "placements": deepcopy(value["placements"]),
            "placement_overlaps": deepcopy(value["placement_overlaps"]),
            "native_execution": deepcopy(value["binding"]["native_execution"]),
            "classification": deepcopy(metadata.get("classification")),
            "original_input_classifications": classifications,
            "source_project_relation": "same_project" if local else "retained_foreign_source"}
    else:
        selection = _json(paths, "selection.json")
        raw = {k: v for k, v in selection.items() if k != "id"}
        binding = _json(paths, "input-binding.json")
        value = _json(paths, "original-native-response.json")
        if (selection.get("schema") != "upstate.terrain-conditioning-report-sources/v1"
                or selection.get("id") != native_id or digest(raw) != native_id
                or selection.get("project_id") != project_id or selection.get("binding") != binding
                or value.get("schema") != "upstate.terrain-native-response/v1"
                or value.get("state") != "complete"
                or selection["response_id"] != value["id"]
                or selection["case_id"] != value["selection"]["case_id"]
                or metadata.get("terrain_conditioning_response_id") != value["id"]
                or metadata.get("terrain_conditioning_case_id") != selection["case_id"]
                or binding["response_id"] != value["id"] or binding["project_id"] != project_id):
            raise ContractError("The terrain evidence differs from its original completed response")
        if local:
            from . import terrain_conditioning_report_source as original
            retained = original.inspect(workspace, native_id)
            if retained.get("state") != "complete" or retained["selection"] != selection or retained["binding"] != binding:
                raise ContractError("The selected source differs from its original native terrain report")
        units = {}
        for row in value["rows"]:
            p = row["metric"]
            if p in units and units[p] != row["units"]:
                raise ContractError("One terrain quantity has inconsistent annual units")
            units[p] = row["units"]
        if set(units) != set(binding["quantity_support"]):
            raise ContractError("The original terrain report lost its complete quantity support")
        result = {"family": family, "id": native_id, "response_id": value["id"],
            "case_id": selection["case_id"], "project_id": project_id,
            "quantity_scope": "original_terrain_joint_native_support",
            "quantities": [{"pollutant": p, "units": units[p]} for p in units],
            "run_ids": [binding["baseline_run_id"], *[r["run_id"] for r in binding["alternatives"]]],
            "geometry": deepcopy(binding["case"]),
            "rows": deepcopy(value["rows"]), "support": deepcopy(binding["quantity_support"]),
            "native_execution": deepcopy(binding["native_versions"]),
            "classification": deepcopy(binding.get("source_classification")),
            "original_input_classifications": deepcopy(binding["original_source_records"]),
            "source_project_relation": "same_project" if local else "retained_foreign_source"}
    result["report_title"] = recipe.get("title", entry.get("title"))
    return result


def describe(workspace, collection_id, source_id):
    collection, entry, paths, source, family, native_id, recipe = _document(
        workspace, collection_id, source_id)
    native = _native(workspace, entry, paths, family, native_id, recipe)
    return {"source": source, "native": native}


def catalog(workspace):
    choices, issues = [], []
    for path in sorted((workspace.root / "sources").glob("*.json")):
        try:
            collection = workspace._get("sources", path.stem)
        except (ValueError, KeyError, OSError, TypeError) as error:
            issues.append({"source_collection_id": path.stem, "message": str(error)})
            continue
        for entry in collection.get("entries", []):
            metadata = entry.get("metadata", {})
            if (entry.get("kind") != "document" or entry.get("role") != "OBSERVED_CONTEXT"
                    or not isinstance(metadata, dict) or not any(k in metadata for k in FAMILIES)):
                continue
            try:
                value = describe(workspace, collection["id"], entry["id"])
                native = value["native"]
                choices.append({"source_collection_id": collection["id"], "source_id": entry["id"],
                    "title": entry.get("title", entry["id"]), "family": native["family"],
                    "project_id": native["project_id"], "native_id": native["id"],
                    "quantities": native["quantities"], "support_scope": native["quantity_scope"],
                    "classification": native["classification"],
                    "source_project_relation": native["source_project_relation"]})
            except (ValueError, KeyError, OSError, ImportError, TypeError) as error:
                issues.append({"source_collection_id": collection["id"], "source_id": entry["id"],
                               "message": str(error)})
    return {"schema": SCHEMA, "choices": choices, "issues": issues, "limitations": LIMITATIONS}


def resolve(workspace, record, selection):
    from .monitoring_recommendations import _context_view
    view = _context_view(record)
    stations = {row["source_station_id"]: row for row in view["stations"]}
    cohorts = {row["id"]: row for row in view["cohorts"]}
    results, cache = {}, {}
    for target in selection["targets"]:
        if "model_evidence" not in target:
            continue
        chosen = normalize(target["model_evidence"])
        key = chosen["source_collection_id"], chosen["source_id"]
        if key not in cache:
            cache[key] = describe(workspace, *key)
        value = deepcopy(cache[key])
        native = value["native"]
        quantities = {q["pollutant"]: q for q in native["quantities"]}
        if chosen["pollutant"] not in quantities:
            raise ContractError("Choose a quantity actually present in the exact selected native source")
        pollutant = chosen["pollutant"]
        native["selected_quantity"] = deepcopy(quantities[pollutant])
        native["support"] = deepcopy(native["support"][pollutant])
        if native["family"] == "control_outcomes":
            native["rows"] = [{**r, "siting_contrasts": {pollutant: r["siting_contrasts"][pollutant]},
                              "native_support": {pollutant: r["native_support"][pollutant]}}
                             for r in native["rows"]]
        else:
            native["rows"] = [r for r in native["rows"] if r["metric"] == pollutant]
        value.update(schema=SCHEMA, selection=chosen, applicability=chosen["applicability"],
            target_binding={"context_id": record["id"], "context_digest": digest(record),
                "network_id": record["network_id"], "network_digest": record["network_digest"],
                "station": deepcopy(stations[target["station_id"]]),
                "cohort": deepcopy(cohorts[target["cohort_id"]]),
                "evidence_start": selection["evidence_start"], "evidence_end": selection["evidence_end"],
                "months": deepcopy(target["months"])},
            relation={"spatial": "not_established", "constituent": "analyst_context_only",
                "temporal": "annual_model_vs_selected_observation_window", "quantitative_comparison": False},
            limitations=deepcopy(LIMITATIONS))
        results[target["id"]] = value
    return results


def export_members(workspace, records):
    from .monitoring_packet import bytes_member, file_member
    seen = set()
    for record in records:
        for target in record["targets"]:
            value = target.get("model_evidence")
            if value is None:
                continue
            source = value["source"]
            key = source["collection_id"], source["source_id"]
            if key in seen:
                continue
            seen.add(key)
            collection, entry, paths, current, _, _, _ = _document(workspace, *key)
            if current != source:
                raise ContractError("The exact saved target evidence changed before export")
            prefix = "native-evidence/" + key[0] + "/" + key[1] + "/"
            yield prefix + "source-edition.json", bytes_member(canonical_bytes(collection))
            yield prefix + "source-entry.json", bytes_member(canonical_bytes(entry))
            for body in [entry["body"], *entry.get("companions", [])]:
                name = _name(body.get("view_path", body["filename"]))
                yield prefix + name, file_member(paths[name], body["bytes"], body["sha256"])


def include(closure, proposal):
    """Original Study resolver owns source objects and all local native histories."""
    for target in proposal.get("targets", []):
        value = target.get("model_evidence")
        if value is None:
            continue
        source = value["source"]
        collection_id, source_id = source["collection_id"], source["source_id"]
        closure.need("sources", collection_id, "Original sampling target native evidence")
        if value["native"]["project_id"] == closure.workspace.project["id"]:
            kind = ("multivariate-control-outcomes" if value["native"]["family"] == "control_outcomes"
                    else "terrain-conditioning-report-sources")
            closure.need(kind, value["native"]["id"],
                         "Complete original native evidence for an explicit sampling target")

# Original observations in Monitoring design

This component joins the existing Monitoring design workspace to retained stream observations, source network relations and historical daily-flow coverage. It uses the current native registry, task queue, immutable records and authenticated exports. A selected network, saved design or campaign revision remains unchanged.

## What the original Eighteenmile data establishes

The retained cohort contains four WQP stations, 589 original nutrient results, 153 station activities on 106 dates, and all 2,192 daily means at USGS 02186702 during 2020–2025. The original high-flow coverage package is the 20-file source cohort merged in PR3167.

Three additional unchanged USGS NLDI upstream-with-tributaries responses establish the indexed order of the selected reaches:

SV375 → SV245 → SV376 → USGS 02186702 → SV233.

For SV375, SV245 and SV376, each original navigation response's station identifier and COMID agrees with the independently retained coordinate hydrolocation. The final gauge–SV233 relation uses their exact shared ReachCode and original measures: gauge 53.4049 and SV233 17.172927977358476. The source linear reference runs from zero at the downstream end to 100 at the upstream end.

The three complete source URLs are:

- https://api.water.usgs.gov/nldi/linked-data/comid/11749145/navigation/UT/wqp?f=json&distance=100
- https://api.water.usgs.gov/nldi/linked-data/comid/11749687/navigation/UT/wqp?f=json&distance=100
- https://api.water.usgs.gov/nldi/linked-data/comid/11749243/navigation/UT/wqp?f=json&distance=100

All responses, their complete properties and original point geometry are retained. The source relation table has 20 ordered pairwise station/gauge relations. Transitive paths list every supporting original response and hydrolocation source. The point layer uses the original WQP station coordinates, retaining indexed reach identity as attributes.

NLDI describes catchment-indexed connectivity. The original unsimplified whole-reach basin remains separate from a precisely split gauge basin. Source points, linear references, travel time and intervening watershed contributions remain distinct.

## Paired chemistry interpretation

The source processor consumes the existing AE11 paired-station table unchanged. It adds network direction, upstream/downstream station IDs and the same interval expressed as downstream minus upstream. Reversing station order exchanges and negates interval endpoints and exchanges the open-end flags. It preserves all original source activity IDs, sample clocks, reported time zones, clock separation, censoring bounds, analytes and source gauge qualifiers.

Across the existing 23 shared dates for SV375 and SV376, phosphorus is higher at the downstream SV376 on 22 dates and unresolved by censoring on one. The 22 include an interval with lower endpoint zero but an open boundary. Reconstructed total nitrogen is lower downstream on 20 dates and higher on three. This is the existing paired source result expressed in original stream order. Same-date sampling is not a travel-time-aligned parcel comparison, and the context makes no source attribution or attenuation estimate.

The existing paired-analysis owner retains leave-one-date-out, year-cohort and high-flow-exclusion sensitivity. This component supplies the source network interpretation to that maintained study.

## Existing desk workflow

1. Import the ordinary application-root manifest, eighteenmile_monitoring_context.sources.json. It registers the observational document, original station point layer and source relation table. Each source carries its complete declared original and derived companion files.
2. Open Monitoring design and select its existing source-bound network. Original source station IDs match exactly. An explicit mapping is available when the network uses a different original identifier.
3. Optionally open a saved design or campaign. A campaign supplies its retained station bindings and exact revision identity.
4. Under Observed support for this network, select the imported source edition and preview.
5. Review the full station-match table, station coordinate differences, selected catchment association, original source topology, exact calendar date overlap, high-flow episodes and signed paired concentration intervals.
6. Save the context. The immutable record retains source, network, plan and campaign revision identities.
7. Download the complete context package or export the existing field package while this saved context and matching plan remain selected.

The original field-package and HTML actions include the selected context only when its exact plan and network match. Campaign exports also require the same original campaign revision. The existing complete Workspace export carries the immutable context and retained source objects through ordinary backup/restore.

Station mapping is explicit. A source activity identifier is never accepted as a station identifier. The module reports every unmatched source station and every native station without observations. A coordinate difference above 100 metres is an inspection flag; the reported distance is a spherical point-to-point diagnostic and does not move either source point.

## Review original station identifiers

When a network uses an agency's short site code and the observational source uses its complete original station identifier, open **Match retained station identifiers** under Observed support. Choose an original network station field, review the proposed source-to-network pairs, then choose **Apply reviewed matches**. The field selector lists retained string properties containing exact source station identifiers; it does not remove prefixes, compare names or infer identity from distance.

Existing explicit mappings are preserved. An exact native station ID already resolves automatically. A repeated field value, an occupied native target or an invalid existing mapping stays visible for review and is not silently replaced. **Clear explicit mapping** resets only the current editable selection; saved contexts retain their original mappings. The original JSON editor remains available for a documented explicit choice.

Applying or clearing mappings invalidates the current preview and its download links. Choose **Preview original support**, inspect station assignments and the unchanged calendar, and **Save this context**. The same source and network digests preserve the original property values behind the mapping in the context's export.

The original 87-station regional assessment edition demonstrates this path: its published `monitoring_location_id` properties match four full microbial WQP IDs, while the native IDs come from `site`: RS-21014, RS-24163, SV-111 and SV-344. These source-field matches cover 117 original observations. USGS-02177000 is absent from that station edition, so its daily flow remains outside this network's station scope. Other networks retain their own exact identifiers and source membership.

## Calendar and event meaning

Calendar overlap uses the saved plan's unchanged absolute dates. It does not transplant a future programme into prior source years.

For each actual saved visit the record carries:

- Exact visit key, catchment search area and date.
- Original campaign station binding when present.
- Matching original source station and same-station/same-date activity IDs.
- Original daily mean, qualifiers, source record indices and annual-P95 membership when that date exists.
- An explicit outside-received-series state when no original day is available.

An unbound catchment remains an unbound search area even when a source station lies in it. Candidate stations in that area are listed separately. A planned date overlapping a high-flow episode is a calendar intersection; collected field-event history remains in the original campaign.

Whole-cohort year/month coverage and matched-station activity counts are labeled separately. The source has 65 annual-P95 episodes; 58 have no sampled day across the four-station cohort. A partial network may have fewer observed stations, and its own episode sample count is reported alongside the full source count.

Daily mean discharge is measured at USGS 02186702. It is regional date context for the four nutrient stations. It is not site-specific discharge for every point and is not multiplied by concentration to create annual mass.

## Public model API

Module: model.monitoring_observed_context.

- catalog(workspace): eligible retained document sources, exact station IDs and source-period counts.
- preview(workspace, **selection): reads original sources and current selected network/plan/campaign; returns a complete unsaved context.
- prepare(workspace, **selection): saves that result in monitoring_observed_contexts using the existing immutable store.
- inspect(workspace, context_id): verifies retained document/companions/manifest, original network sources, saved plan identity and exact historical campaign revision.
- list_saved(workspace): immutable context summaries.
- export_files(workspace, context_id, plan_id=None, network_id=None): exact context, CSV tables, human report and original source closure for the existing field package.
- export_context(workspace, context_id, export_root=None): complete original ZIP through the same authenticated queued export.
- verify_workspace(workspace): original object/relation verification on native receiving.

Selection keys:

    {
      "source_collection_id": "ACTUAL_IMPORTED_COLLECTION",
      "source_id": "eighteenmile-monitoring-observed-context-20261013",
      "network_id": "ACTUAL_SAVED_NETWORK",
      "plan_id": "ACTUAL_SAVED_PLAN",
      "station_mapping": {},
      "title": "Observed support for the selected monitoring plan"
    }

Choose plan_id or campaign_id. A network-only context is also supported. The actual returned native IDs come from the original Workspace; the source package supplies no fabricated IDs.

Queue writes are monitoring.context.prepare and monitoring.context.export. Existing GET /api/monitoring reads are context.catalog, context.list, context.get and context.preview. The established monitoring.export accepts optional context_id. The current 1.2.1 queued-export selection/completion record, expected campaign revision, workspace lock and task file decoration are preserved.

Source schemas: upstate.monitoring-observed-source/v1 (retained nutrient context) and upstate.monitoring-observed-source/v2 (explicit station flow scope).
Source role: monitoring_observed_context.
Saved result schema: upstate.monitoring_observed_contexts/v1 (the native Workspace collection schema).
Collection: monitoring_observed_contexts.

## Station-specific microbial observations

The original microbial source is selected through `microbial_monitoring_context.sources.json`. Its complete source document uses `upstate.monitoring-observed-source/v2` and retains the 36-station, 730-observation cohort under `source/ecoli_temporal_analysis/20261013/monitoring-context/`. The original Eighteenmile nutrient document remains version 1 and retains its existing regional date-context interpretation.

Version 2 requires an explicit flow scope:

```json
{
  "mode": "same_station_only",
  "gauge_station_id": "USGS-02177000",
  "station_ids": ["USGS-02177000"],
  "start_inclusive": "2022-01-01",
  "end_inclusive": "2022-12-31"
}
```

The saved calendar receives Chattooga daily discharge only when its original campaign binding resolves to that exact source station and its date lies within the declared scope. An unbound visit has `station_not_bound_to_source`; another station has `station_outside_flow_scope`; a date beyond the declared period has `date_outside_flow_scope`. An eligible date missing from the original daily table remains `outside_received_daily_series`. Those states retain null discharge and threshold fields. A coincident sampling date at another station never supplies station-specific Chattooga flow.

Episode activity support uses only matched, in-scope `Sample-Routine` activities. The retained `Quality Control Sample-Field Replicate` remains an original observation and activity, while episode sampling coverage excludes it. Calendar episode overlap likewise requires the original scoped station/date. A selected network without the source gauge has no applicable matched-station unsampled-episode statistic; full original-source episode counts remain separately labeled.

Both source versions are accepted by the current receiver. Version 1 may retain its legacy unscoped regional date context. A version 2 source without a scope is rejected. Using a new source version ensures an earlier version-1-only receiver cannot silently apply the new microbial gauge data across the whole station cohort.

### Original station datum

Source coordinates can declare `WGS84` or `NAD83`. Every station match retains `original_longitude`, `original_latitude` and `original_datum`. Exact identifier or explicit station mapping remains available for both datums.

The two original NAD83 microbial stations retain that declaration. Their comparison to a WGS84 native station is marked `different_datum`, and `coordinate_difference_m` is null. The adapter performs no implicit datum transformation or relabeling. WGS84-to-WGS84 coordinates retain the existing spherical distance diagnostic and 100-metre review flag.

### Complete observed records

The optional source `observations` table binds each unique `observation_id` to an existing source station/activity/date. For the microbial source, the identity is the original source filename plus `#row=` and its one-based source row. The saved context preserves every matched-station observation as the complete unchanged source row.

Original reported results, detection limits, statuses, methods, units, interval endpoints, sample clocks/time zones, activity types, comments and comment flags remain available. A null upper bound with `upper_unbounded: true` is an unbounded censoring interval; a missing reported value remains missing. The adapter does not replace censored values with zero, combine distinct activities, convert original units, or attribute load from concentration.

The Monitoring desk offers station, original-status and comment filters, pages of 50 records, and an Inspect control for each complete original row. Filters affect only the display. Summary counts distinguish the full source from matched stations. The original full-context JSON, report, standalone ZIP, campaign field package and report-source bridge carry `observed-context/observations.csv` with all fields from every matched observation. The original document and all retained companions remain in the same export source closure. A historical saved context without an observations table keeps its original report columns, sections and export member set; a new context retains observations.csv even when its matched subset is empty.

### Adopt and receive the complete update

Use the same `integrations/monitoring/install_observed_context.py` installer and existing extension registration. Its source inventory contains byte counts, hashes and allowed published predecessors. It snapshots the manifest and each validated source body, compiles those exact Python bytes, then atomically writes the same postimages. A concurrently changed target or target manifest is rejected without substituting newly read, unverified source bytes.

Import the microbial manifest into the original receiving Workspace, then use the existing `observed_context` selection with its actual imported source ID and existing network/plan/campaign. Prepare, inspect and export through the ordinary Monitoring commands. The same `operator/monitoring_receiving.py` route reopens the source and saved context after Workspace transfer. Review one gauge-bound 2022 visit and one other-station visit: only the first can carry original Chattooga discharge. Review a NAD83 station and an unbounded result through Inspect and the exported source rows.

## Reproduce the source context

From the current complete application:

    node source/eighteenmile-stream-nutrients-20261013/monitoring-context/derive-monitoring-context.mjs

The processor checks every input's byte length and SHA-256 before writing its five derived outputs. It uses the exact original-network edition, the merged flow-coverage cohort and the maintained paired-study CSV. It adds three unchanged agency responses. The input manifest records those source identities.

To inspect in a native existing Workspace:

    python -B -m model.cli --workspace "$WORKSPACE" source-import eighteenmile_monitoring_context.sources.json
    python -B -m model.monitoring_observed_context --workspace "$WORKSPACE" catalog
    python -B -m model.monitoring_observed_context --workspace "$WORKSPACE" preview --selection "$SELECTION" --output "$PREVIEW"
    python -B -m model.monitoring_observed_context --workspace "$WORKSPACE" prepare --selection "$SELECTION" --output "$RECEIPT"

Use the actual retained network/plan/campaign and source collection IDs in the selection. Open that same context in Monitoring design, export the context and existing field package, then receive the ordinary complete Workspace and reopen the saved result.

## Complete source adoption

A full current checkout already includes the addon. For a maintained application with the shared extension registry, use:

    python -B integrations/monitoring/install_observed_context.py --application "$APPLICATION" --source "$SOURCE_ROOT" --preview
    python -B integrations/monitoring/install_observed_context.py --application "$APPLICATION" --source "$SOURCE_ROOT"

The installer checks every supplied body against the complete source manifest and every replacement against its current known predecessor. Existing 1.2.1 revisions/locks, export-intent records, source verification and workspace-scoped browser refresh remain composed. Original standalone archive members and their 1.2.0 manifest remain historical originals; runtime composition is recorded separately.

The source module parses original CSVs and resolves graph relations in the source-analysis runtime. Native preview/save/export requires the actual installed MonitoringWorkspace. Browser modules have been parsed in V8 and retain current shared-provider contracts. Actual native execution results belong to the receiving operation and its returned Workspace IDs.

## Primary method references

- USGS NLDI navigation: https://api.water.usgs.gov/docs/nldi/navigation/
- USGS NHD linear referencing: https://pubs.usgs.gov/fs/2012/3068/
- Original WQP station/result sources and complete source hashes: source/eighteenmile-stream-nutrients-20261013/source-manifest.json.
- Existing paired source: observations/eighteenmile_stream_nutrients_2020_2025/analysis/paired-station-contrasts.csv.
- Original flow coverage: source/eighteenmile-stream-nutrients-20261013/flow-analysis/input-manifest.json.

## Open an immutable context from Study transfer

Use **Open in Monitoring** on an observational-context row in the original Study transfer catalogue. The desk reads that exact context and its bound network, then opens the existing Saved context controls. This supports both network-only contexts and contexts containing an earlier saved sampling calendar. The earlier calendar stays in the context; the current campaign is not substituted for it.

The context opens with no new design or campaign selected. Its original observation filters, station matches, detailed source identity and complete package export work immediately. To calculate another preview, explicitly choose the desired retained design or campaign first. Switching networks clears old selection labels and download links. Pending openings are discarded if the Workspace or active Monitoring desk changes.

"""Stream exact original Monitoring source members into a retained field package.

The packet keeps its original deterministic ZIP member names and metadata. Large
native files stay on disk; every streamed body must match its source descriptor.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import hashlib
import os
from pathlib import Path, PurePosixPath
import tempfile
import time
import zipfile

from .monitoring_common import ContractError

CHUNK_BYTES = 1024 * 1024


def bytes_member(body):
    if not isinstance(body, bytes):
        raise TypeError("Retain canonical packet metadata as bytes")
    return {"content": body, "bytes": len(body),
            "sha256": hashlib.sha256(body).hexdigest()}


def file_member(path, size, sha256):
    return {"file": Path(path), "bytes": size, "sha256": sha256}


def _member_name(name):
    path = PurePosixPath(name)
    if (not isinstance(name, str) or path.is_absolute() or not path.parts
            or path.as_posix() != name or ".." in path.parts
            or "\\" in name or "\0" in name):
        raise ContractError("The original source packet member leaves its directory")
    return name


def add_member(files, name, member):
    name = _member_name(name)
    previous = files.get(name)
    if previous is not None and any(previous[key] != member[key]
                                    for key in ("bytes", "sha256")):
        raise ContractError("Original monitoring packet members conflict")
    files[name] = member


def _identity(stat):
    return tuple(getattr(stat, field) for field in
                 ("st_dev", "st_ino", "st_size", "st_mtime_ns", "st_ctime_ns"))


def _copy_body(member, outgoing):
    checksum, size = hashlib.sha256(), 0
    if "content" in member:
        body = member["content"]
        checksum.update(body)
        size = len(body)
        outgoing.write(body)
    else:
        path = member["file"]
        if path.is_symlink() or not path.is_file():
            raise ContractError("The original packet member must be an ordinary file")
        with path.open("rb") as incoming:
            before = os.fstat(incoming.fileno())
            for body in iter(lambda: incoming.read(CHUNK_BYTES), b""):
                checksum.update(body)
                size += len(body)
                outgoing.write(body)
            after = os.fstat(incoming.fileno())
        if _identity(before) != _identity(after):
            raise ContractError("Original source changed while streaming its packet")
    if size != member["bytes"] or checksum.hexdigest() != member["sha256"]:
        raise ContractError("Original source bytes changed while streaming their packet")


def _packet_identity(path):
    if path.is_symlink() or not path.is_file():
        raise ContractError("The retained source packet must be an ordinary file")
    with path.open("rb") as stream:
        before = os.fstat(stream.fileno())
        checksum = hashlib.sha256()
        size = 0
        for body in iter(lambda: stream.read(CHUNK_BYTES), b""):
            checksum.update(body)
            size += len(body)
        after = os.fstat(stream.fileno())
    if _identity(before) != _identity(after) or size != after.st_size:
        raise ContractError("The retained source packet changed while being read")
    return {"path": path, "bytes": size, "sha256": checksum.hexdigest()}


def _verify_existing(path, files):
    """Recover a fully published packet after interruption before plan saving."""
    result = _packet_identity(path)
    with zipfile.ZipFile(path) as archive:
        names = archive.namelist()
        if len(names) != len(set(names)) or set(names) != set(files):
            raise ContractError("The retained campaign packet has another member inventory")
        for name, member in files.items():
            checksum, size = hashlib.sha256(), 0
            with archive.open(name) as incoming:
                for body in iter(lambda: incoming.read(CHUNK_BYTES), b""):
                    checksum.update(body)
                    size += len(body)
            if size != member["bytes"] or checksum.hexdigest() != member["sha256"]:
                raise ContractError("The retained campaign packet member differs: " + name)
    if _packet_identity(path) != result:
        raise ContractError("The retained campaign packet changed during recovery")
    return result


def retain_packet(path, files, *, metadata="deterministic"):
    """Publish an exact source-bound ZIP; retain handoff or ordinary export metadata.

    Existing fieldwork packets keep their deterministic defaults. Review exports
    use the original ZipFile.writestr timestamp and regular-file permissions.
    """
    if metadata not in {"deterministic", "export"}:
        raise ValueError("Choose deterministic handoff or ordinary export ZIP metadata")
    path = Path(path)
    files = {_member_name(name): member for name, member in files.items()}
    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    if path.exists() or path.is_symlink():
        return _verify_existing(path, files)
    pending = None
    try:
        with tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile(prefix=".monitoring-packet-", suffix=".zip",
                                         dir=path.parent, delete=False) as stream:
            pending = Path(stream.name)
            with zipfile.ZipFile(stream, "w", compression=zipfile.ZIP_DEFLATED) as archive:
                for name, member in sorted(files.items()):
                    stamp = (1980, 1, 1, 0, 0, 0) if metadata == "deterministic" else time.localtime()[:6]
                    entry = zipfile.ZipInfo(name, date_time=stamp)
                    entry.compress_type = zipfile.ZIP_DEFLATED
                    entry.external_attr = (0o100644 if metadata == "deterministic" else 0o600) << 16
                    entry.file_size = member["bytes"]
                    with archive.open(entry, "w") as outgoing:
                        _copy_body(member, outgoing)
            stream.flush()
            os.fsync(stream.fileno())
        result = _packet_identity(pending)
        try:
            os.link(pending, path)
        except FileExistsError:
            result = _verify_existing(path, files)
        else:
            result["path"] = path
        pending.unlink()
        pending = None
        if os.name != "nt":
            descriptor = os.open(path.parent, os.O_RDONLY | getattr(os, "O_DIRECTORY", 0))
            try:
                os.fsync(descriptor)
            finally:
                os.close(descriptor)
        return result
    finally:
        if pending is not None:
            pending.unlink(missing_ok=True)

# Sampling recommendations in the existing Monitoring application

This component turns an already saved observed context into an editable proposed sampling programme. It retains the exact original observations, station identities, source edition, analytical cohorts, historical period, calendar and network. It uses the maintained Monitoring solver for an explicitly requested future design. It adds no observations and no second solver.

## Operator course

1. Open **Sampling priorities**, choose a saved observed context and inspect its original source period, source station matches and exact analytical cohorts. The source picker exposes the currently retained context; it does not issue a public-data request.
2. Enter the programme title, person recording the proposal, actual recording timestamp and planning rationale. Select an evidence window contained within the source's published period.
3. Add a target with an original station and an exact retained cohort. Choose months, a historical minimum of distinct observation dates per month, and a separate proposed number of future visits. The historical minimum applies across the selected evidence window, not separately to every year. The report exposes the dates and years so the interpretation stays inspectable.
4. Enter any proposed reporting-limit target in the unchanged cohort unit, with its explicit rationale. Unknown original reporting limits and incompatible limit units stay visible. No censored value is replaced with zero, half a limit or a generated concentration.
5. Choose any-flow or high-flow intent. Historical event coverage applies only when the retained source explicitly declares the same station and period as the gauge. Nearby stations do not inherit that flow. Future fixed dates do not guarantee a storm.
6. Enter setup and per-visit costs as exact USD decimal strings, or leave them unknown. Zero is an explicit zero. State the cost source or operator assumption. The proposal sums each included target separately; overlapping visits are not automatically discounted.
7. Preview complete station/month support, original observation IDs and rows, reporting limits, source warnings and the proposed budget. Priority is an operator ranking; it is not calculated information gain. Optional sensitivity context is attributed prose, not an inferred match to an unrelated model.
8. Save the immutable proposal. Editing a saved proposal creates a child edition using its exact native ID; the original remains available. The source context is fixed within one proposal family.
9. To request a native design, supply the complete native configuration and include the selected targets' catchments in its explicit required_ids. Resolve unbound stations and multiple stations assigned to one catchment first. Unknown proposal costs may remain unknown when the native configuration supplies its own complete explicit costs; the two budgets stay separate. Set a future calendar after the historical evidence window, with the actual budget, costs, visit lengths, crews and dates. The unchanged native solver owns feasibility, calendar capacity and geographic objective.
10. Read the returned native plan and each target's actual selected-month visit count. The native design has its own entered budget and cost table, shown separately from the itemized proposal estimate. Laboratory analyte/limit requirements and event-triggered work remain explicit planned scope. Creating a plan creates no collected field event.
11. Export the complete proposal bundle, open its readable report and CSVs, and inspect the exact original source files. For an independently editable receiving application, export the original complete Study/Workspace through the current application and reopen that archive. The report ZIP is not a replacement Workspace.

## Model API

All functions are in model.monitoring_recommendations.

- catalog(workspace): observed-context summaries and saved proposal summaries.
- context(workspace, context_id): exact source/station/cohort catalogue. design_configuration is the original saved plan's unchanged configuration when available, otherwise null.
- preview(workspace, *, selection): compute the full proposal without writing.
- prepare(workspace, *, selection, operation_id, parent_id=None, expected_parent_digest=None): save an immutable proposal. For a successor set both parent_id and expected_parent_digest to the exact native parent.id.
- inspect(workspace, recommendation_id): reopen and compare the complete saved calculation with its retained context.
- list_saved(workspace), history(workspace, recommendation_id), designs(workspace, recommendation_id), inspect_design(workspace, design_id).
- design(workspace, *, recommendation_id, configuration, operation_id, title=None): run the original monitoring_design.solve_design and retain the exact plan/result.
- report_html(record, native_designs=None): complete readable report.
- export_members(workspace, recommendation_id): streamable complete-member descriptors for source/package composition.
- export_recommendations(workspace, *, recommendation_id, export_root=None): original file-ticket-compatible path/bytes/SHA result.
- verify_workspace(workspace): inspect retained proposals and native design/source identities.
- compile_recommendations(record, selection): pure calculation from an already inspected full context; useful to a source-native receiving course.

## Exact selection shape

selection contains context_id, title, operator, recorded_at (ISO timestamp with timezone), evidence_start/evidence_end (YYYY-MM-DD), notes, planning_basis and targets.

Every target has:

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| id | Stable explicit target ID, unique within the proposal |
| station_id | Exact source_station_id from the context |
| cohort_id | Exact cohort ID from the context catalogue |
| months | Nonempty distinct integers 1–12 |
| minimum_dates_per_month | Nonnegative historical date-count goal across the selected evidence window |
| proposed_visits | Nonnegative future planning count |
| reporting_limit | Null or nonnegative exact decimal string in the cohort's original unit |
| reporting_limit_basis | Explicit scientific/operator rationale |
| flow_goal | any or high_flow |
| reason | Concrete purpose of the target |
| priority | Operator-entered integer 1–5 |
| included | Boolean; excluded targets remain saved and visible |
| setup_cost / per_visit_cost | Null or exact USD amount string, at most two decimal places |
| cost_basis | Published source or explicit operator planning assumption |
| sensitivity_basis | Optional source-qualified narrative; no automatic information-gain calculation |

Cohort identity retains both field presence and value. Missing, null and empty metadata remain distinct. Characteristic, method, unit, fraction, value type, speciation and available method/media/depth/project metadata participate. Original concentration values and source record IDs do not split a cohort; every original row remains retained.

Output targets preserve their full input under target, the original station match, complete cohort fields, original evidence rows and IDs, monthly gaps, reporting-limit comparisons, exact flow applicability, itemized costs and warnings. The top-level gaps array is the complete monthly table. budget splits known_total_cents from unknown_target_ids. handoff preserves required_catchment_ids, unbound_target_ids, station_binding_conflicts, station_bindings and complete included requirements.

## Native persistence and retries

Immutable collections:

- monitoring_recommendations: source-bound proposal editions and parent ancestry.
- monitoring_recommendation_designs: proposal-to-original-native-plan selections/results.
- monitoring_plans: existing authoritative solver plans.

The small monitoring_recommendation_operations index is operation recovery, not a second scientific store. Exact retries return the original immutable result. Reusing an operation ID for another payload fails. Interrupted publication after an immutable save is recovered by the original operation marker. Native solver plans retain their recommendation operation/fingerprint so a crash before the result index does not repeat the solved design.

The original Workspace _save/_get methods own content addressing. The source context, network and plan are checked through their maintained original readers. No live source, running worker, original observation or old plan is overwritten.

## Native CLI

From the existing application root, use its compatible GIS Python:

    GIS_PYTHON -m model.monitoring_recommendations --workspace WORKSPACE catalog --output catalog.json
    GIS_PYTHON -m model.monitoring_recommendations --workspace WORKSPACE context --request context-request.json --output context.json
    GIS_PYTHON -m model.monitoring_recommendations --workspace WORKSPACE preview --request preview-request.json --output preview.json
    GIS_PYTHON -m model.monitoring_recommendations --workspace WORKSPACE prepare --request prepare-request.json --output saved.json
    GIS_PYTHON -m model.monitoring_recommendations --workspace WORKSPACE design --request design-request.json --output design.json
    GIS_PYTHON -m model.monitoring_recommendations --workspace WORKSPACE export --request export-request.json --output export.json

Request JSON uses the same named keyword arguments as the functions. The existing queued operator injects its actual task ID as operation_id. It preserves one operation across response loss and reload.

## Complete producing and receiving course

Use one actual retained context in the original received application; prefer the physically received Eighteenmile source cohort where already admitted. Do not manufacture an observed source to make the screen populated. If the source has not yet been bound to a saved network, use the existing context intake and exact original station mapping first.

Create an explicitly authored proposal using those real rows. Inspect one fully observed station/cohort and one month with no retained match; choose costs and goals as visibly authored planning assumptions. Save it, change a target, save a child edition and reopen both. Repeat the identical save operation and confirm the same immutable ID; a different payload under that operation must not create a new proposal.

Request a native design using the retained network and complete explicit future configuration. Read the original solver status, cost, selected catchments and calendar, alongside target-specific future counts. If infeasible, retain the actual result and make an explicit revised selection/configuration; do not disguise it as a successful calendar.

Operate the current application at desktop and390px, personally inspect both views, and use source selection, target edits, preview/save, saved history, design, report/export and fresh reopening. Open every generated HTML/CSV/JSON/source attachment and the full exported archive. Resolve actual visible errors in this same source. Preserve all existing scientific runs, the actual equipped receiving owner and the current AGENTS.md / CURRENT_OWNER_DIRECTION.md instructions. Warm correspondence remains with its original owner and Bryce's exact-message authorization.

Return the real runtime/source paths, exact saved context/proposal/design IDs, current source head, native result and actual rendered files to ECO-SAMPLING-15227-20261013 in the original Eco thread. Source construction and a retained Git blob alone are not a claim that this native course ran.

## One complete same-operation native course

The maintained source_tools/receive_sampling_recommendations.py accepts the exact authored inputs, executes the existing solver, exports the source-bound report and selected Study, restores it through model.portable.resume_restore and independently reopens the same complete proposal/design. It then recovers the original save operation from the immutable records in that fresh Workspace. Its output is outside the live Workspace and exact input files are preserved before work.

    GIS_PYTHON source_tools/receive_sampling_recommendations.py --workspace WORKSPACE --selection SELECTION.json --successor-selection SUCCESSOR.json --design-configuration NATIVE_CONFIGURATION.json --operation-id ECO-SAMPLING-15227-COURSE --output NEW_OPERATION_DIRECTORY

The successor input is optional; all other arguments select the real existing source and explicit planning intent. An infeasible native result remains an actual result. This command creates no historical observations, sends no message and starts no replacement server. Complete GUI and attachment operation follows in the same received application.
